key_insight: Reactive sputtering can produce epitaxial Mn4N thin films with strong perpendicular magnetic anisotropy and current-driven switching, making Mn4N a viable rare-earth-free spintronic material.
engineering_relevance: Optimized Mn4N/Pt films offer a scalable route to low-power spin-orbit torque devices with tunable coercivity and robust anomalous Hall response.
method: Reactive magnetron sputtering of Mn4N on MgO(100) and SrTiO3(100)
Structural, magnetic, and magnetotransport characterization of film quality and anisotropy
Density functional theory to assess the role of strain and interfacial effects
evidence_signal: The optimized films show epitaxial growth on MgO, square hysteresis loops with high remanence, strong anomalous Hall effect, and efficient current-induced switching in Mn4N/Pt bilayers.
watch_item: Perpendicular magnetic anisotropy depends not only on strain but also on interface quality, so reproducibility may be sensitive to deposition and layer control.
paper_title: Optimization of Epitaxial Mn4N Thin Films Grown by Sputtering for Spintronic Applications
